title: Exploring the Studica Robotics Kit
objective: Unbox and inventory every structural aluminum channel, bracket, and fastener in your Studica Robotics Kit, learn the essential laboratory safety rules, and master the use of vibration-resistant Nyloc hex nuts.
exitTicket: What is the function of the colored nylon collar inside an M4 Nyloc nut, and what physical effect does it have during robot motion?
Why must standard hex nuts never be used on motor mounts or structural drive joints?
State the three essential laboratory safety rules that must always be followed before turning on any robot in the lab.
concept:
1. Welcome to Physical Autonomous Mobile Robotics

Welcome to the hands-on engineering world of Autonomous Mobile Robotics! Over the course of this training program, you will build, wire, program, and operate a fully autonomous robot capable of precision navigation, sensor feedback, and real-time obstacle avoidance.

Our educational philosophy is strictly Hands-on First:

Build First → Experience → Understand → Program → Improve → Automate

Before writing a single line of Python code, we must construct a rock-solid mechanical foundation. A software algorithm cannot compensate for a loose motor mount or a vibrating chassis!

2. Structural Extrusions: Why Aluminum U-Channels?

The robot skeleton is engineered from 6061-T6 structural aluminum U-channels. Aluminum provides three critical advantages for mobile robots:

  • High Strength-to-Weight Ratio: Stiff enough to support heavy 12V batteries and manipulators without bending, yet light enough to maximize battery runtime and motor acceleration.
  • Standard Metric 8mm Pitch Grid: Holes are spaced exactly 8mm apart with 16mm center-to-center hole patterns, allowing modular brackets, bearings, and motors to snap together perfectly.
  • Internal Wire Channels: The U-shape profile allows high-current motor cables and sensor harnesses to run inside the channel, shielding wires from pinch points and moving wheels.
💡 PRO-TIP: THE BLUE COLLAR OF SAFETY (NYLOC NUTS)
Standard hex nuts will shake completely loose after just 10 minutes of robot driving due to high-frequency motor vibrations! Always use Nyloc locknuts on every structural joint and motor mount. You can identify them instantly by the colored nylon ring (usually blue or white) embedded inside the threaded collar.
⚠️ MANDATORY LABORATORY SAFETY RULES
  • Safety Glasses: Always wear ANSI Z87.1 certified eye protection when using wrenches, assembling mechanical springs, or rotating motors.
  • Battery Safety: Never connect or disconnect battery leads while the main robot power switch is toggled ON. Turn power OFF first!
  • Clothing & Hair: Keep long hair tied back firmly, remove dangling lanyard badges, and roll up loose sleeves before working near rotating gears or wheels.
🔧 TROUBLESHOOTING: STRIPPED HEADS & CROSS-THREADING
If an M4 screw feels tight after only 1 or 2 turns, STOP IMMEDIATELY! Never force it with pliers. You have cross-threaded the bolt. Back the screw out completely, align it perpendicular ($90^\circ$) to the channel hole, and start threading gently by hand using your fingers before tightening with the 2.5mm hex key.

title: Understanding the Robot Controller
objective: Understand how your robot thinks and acts by exploring the dual-controller architecture: Raspberry Pi 4 (high-level Linux/ROS 2 computer), VMX-pi (real-time FPGA reflexes and navX IMU), and Titan Quad (high-power motor driver over 1 Mbps CAN bus).
exitTicket: Why can a standard operating system like Linux not guarantee microsecond motor timing directly, necessitating an FPGA coprocessor?
What are the two signal lines in a CAN bus cable, and why are they twisted tightly together?
Which VMX-pi port group is used for high-current LEDs, and which port group is used for push buttons and limit switches?
concept:
1. The Dual-Brain Architecture: Brain & Muscle

Modern autonomous mobile robots require two completely different computational worlds to operate successfully:

  1. High-Level Compute Brain (Raspberry Pi 4): Runs Ubuntu Linux 22.04 and ROS 2 Humble. It processes complex algorithms such as LiDAR floor mapping, computer vision, path planning, and Wi-Fi teleoperation. However, standard Linux is non-deterministic: background OS tasks can delay code execution by milliseconds.
  2. Real-Time Microsecond Reflexes (VMX-pi FPGA): Contains a dedicated Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) that executes timing-critical pulses, hardware quadrature encoder counting, and hardware interrupts with microsecond precision. It also houses the integrated 9-axis navX Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU).
  3. High-Current Muscle (Titan Quad Motor Controller): An industrial 4-channel H-bridge driver capable of delivering 20A continuous power to 12V DC drive motors. It communicates with the VMX-pi over a high-speed Controller Area Network (CAN bus) operating at 1,000,000 bits per second (1 Mbps).
💡 PRO-TIP: TWISTED PAIR PHYSICS (WHY CAN WIRES ARE TWISTED)
Notice that the Yellow (CAN_H) and Green (CAN_L) wires are twisted tightly around each other! When high-current DC motors spin up, they emit electromagnetic noise (EMI). Because the two wires are twisted, any electromagnetic spike hits both wires equally. The differential CAN receiver subtracts the two signals ($(V_{CAN\_H} - V_{CAN\_L})$), canceling the noise completely and preventing motor commands from being corrupted!
⚠️ SEGREGATED VOLTAGE RAILS (NEVER MIX 12V & 5V)
The Titan Quad operates at full 12V DC battery voltage to supply motor muscle. The VMX-pi and Raspberry Pi operate at 5.0V / 3.3V logic level. Never connect 12V power leads into any VMX-pi DIO or analog header! Doing so will permanently destroy the FPGA and Raspberry Pi processor.
🔧 TROUBLESHOOTING: TITAN STATUS LED FLASHING RED
If the Titan Quad status LED blinks rapidly in RED:
  • Check CAN bus termination: Ensure the tiny 120-ohm termination slider switch on top of the Titan is set firmly to ON.
  • Verify wire polarity: Yellow wire must go to CAN_H and Green wire must go to CAN_L. If reversed, the CAN transceivers cannot handshake.
  • CAN ID Mismatch: In our robotics stack, the primary drive Titan is hardcoded to CAN ID 42. If set to a different ID, ROS 2 motor nodes cannot discover it.

title: Building the Robot Chassis
objective: Assemble the rigid 24cm x 18cm structural aluminum chassis, install 90-degree corner gusset plates, mount standoffs, and verify geometric squareness with diagonal caliper measurement.
exitTicket: What are the target dimensions (Length, Width, Height) of your robot chassis?
Why must both diagonal measurements (from corner A to D, and B to C) match within ±0.5 mm?
What happens if a chassis is assembled as a parallelogram instead of a square when motors drive forward?
concept:
1. Engineering the Chassis Frame

A mobile robot chassis is not merely a box—it is a precision geometric platform. If the chassis frame is distorted into a parallelogram by even 1 millimeter, the robot will naturally veer to one side when driving forward, forcing software controllers to fight mechanical drift continuously.

Our chassis is engineered with compact, balanced dimensions:

  • Overall Length: $240\,\text{mm}\;(24.0\,\text{cm})$
  • Overall Width: $180\,\text{mm}\;(18.0\,\text{cm})$
  • Base Height Clearance: $100\,\text{mm}\;(10.0\,\text{cm})$
         +------------------ 180 mm -------------------+
         |                                             |
         |    [Front Bumper / Sensor Mount Plate]      |
         |                                             |
   240   |   [Left Motor]             [Right Motor]    |
   mm    |      (M0)                      (M1)         |
         |                                             |
         |         [Electronics Mounting Deck]         |
         |                                             |
         |              [Rear Omni Caster]             |
         |      [Ch 9 Limit]          [Ch 10 Limit]    |
         +---------------------------------------------+
💡 PRO-TIP: FINGER-TIGHTEN FIRST, SQUEEZE, THEN TORQUE
Never fully tighten corner bolts one by one! Thread all 8 corner bolts finger-tight so the frame can still shift slightly. Measure both diagonals with your steel ruler until they match within $\pm 0.5\,\text{mm}$. Then, and only then, tighten each bolt in an alternating crisscross pattern.
⚠️ NYLON STANDOFF CAUTION
The acrylic electronics deck is mounted on M3 nylon standoffs to isolate sensitive computer electronics from metal frame vibrations. Never use pliers or metal wrenches on nylon standoffs! Finger-tighten only; excessive torque will shear the nylon threads immediately.
🔧 TROUBLESHOOTING: CHASSIS ROCKS ON TABLE
Place your assembled chassis on a flat marble plate or level table. Press down on opposite diagonal corners. If you feel any rocking motion, your frame is warped:
  1. Loosen all 8 corner gusset screws by half a turn.
  2. Press firmly down on the center of the frame against the flat table with your palm.
  3. While holding the frame flat, have your lab partner retighten the corner bolts in an X-pattern.
wiring:
1. Chassis Assembly Step-by-Step Procedure

  1. Prepare Extrusion Channels: Lay out two 240mm side channels and two 180mm cross channels on your workbench.
  2. Mount 90-Degree Gusset Plates: Position the triangular aluminum gusset plates on the inside corners of the frame. Insert M4x12mm socket-head bolts through the gusset holes into the channels.
  3. Thread Nyloc Hex Nuts: Thread M4 Nyloc nuts onto the bolts from inside the channel. Turn until finger-tight.
  4. Diagonal Squaring Audit: Measure from Top-Left to Bottom-Right ($D_1$), then Top-Right to Bottom-Left ($D_2$). Adjust until $D_1 = D_2 \pm 0.5\,\text{mm}$.
  5. Torque Down: Firmly tighten all 8 bolts using your 2.5mm hex wrench and 7mm nut driver.
  6. Install Standoffs & Deck: Thread four M3×20mm standoffs into the pre-drilled holes on the upper channel flange. Bolt the laser-cut acrylic electronics deck onto the standoffs with M3 button screws.

# Calculate chassis diagonal squareness mathematically:
# Theoretical Diagonal D = sqrt(L^2 + W^2)
# D = sqrt(240^2 + 180^2) = sqrt(57600 + 32400) = sqrt(90000) = 300.00 mm!

python3 -c '
import math
L, W = 240.0, 180.0
theoretical = math.sqrt(L**2 + W**2)
print(f"Target Diagonal = {theoretical:.2f} mm")
'
# Output: Target Diagonal = 300.00 mm (Both diagonals must be exactly 30 cm!)

title: Installing Motors and Wheels
objective: Mount the two 12V 60:1 Maverick planetary gearmotors, align the D-shaft hex wheel couplers, install 100mm high-traction rubber drive wheels, attach the rear omni caster, and derive the 1680 ticks/rev encoder formula.
exitTicket: What is the gear reduction ratio of the Maverick planetary motor, and why is high gear reduction needed for mobile robotics?
Calculate the total encoder ticks per full revolution of the 100mm wheel (Show formula: 28 raw pulses × 60 gear reduction).
Why must blue threadlocker be applied to the set screw on the motor D-shaft hex hub?
concept:
1. Drivetrain Engineering: Torque vs. Speed

Electric DC motors naturally spin very fast (thousands of revolutions per minute) but produce very little turning force (torque). If you connected a bare DC motor directly to a robot wheel, the motor would stall instantly under the robot's weight!

To multiply turning torque, we use a planetary gearbox with a 60:1 reduction ratio. The internal sun and planet gears slow down the motor shaft by a factor of 60 while multiplying output torque by 60, allowing the robot to carry payloads, climb ramps, and accelerate smoothly.

2. Optical Quadrature Encoders: 1680 Ticks Per Turn

On the rear shaft of each Maverick motor sits a magnetic Hall-effect quadrature encoder disc that outputs 28 raw pulses per motor turn. Because the gearbox multiplies every turn by 60:

$$\text{Encoder Resolution} = 28 \times 60 = 1,680\,\text{ticks per wheel revolution}$$

3. Differential Drive Kinematics & Wheel Circumference

Our drive wheels have an outer diameter of $D = 100\,\text{mm}\;(0.100\,\text{m})$. The distance the robot travels forward in one full wheel rotation equals the wheel's circumference ($C$):

$$C = \pi \times D = 3.14159 \times 100\,\text{mm} \approx 314.16\,\text{mm}\;(0.31416\,\text{m})$$

Therefore, the distance traveled per single encoder tick is:

$$\text{Distance Per Tick} = \frac{314.16\,\text{mm}}{1680\,\text{ticks}} \approx 0.187\,\text{mm per tick}$$

With 0.187 mm resolution, your robot can measure its position across the floor down to a fraction of a millimeter!

💡 PRO-TIP: D-SHAFT FLAT ALIGNMENT & THREADLOCKER
The motor output shaft is a 6mm "D-shaft"—it has one flat side. Always position the hex hub set screw directly perpendicular to the flat face! If you tighten the screw against the curved edge, it will slip under load within minutes. Apply one drop of blue threadlocker (Loctite 242) to the set screw threads so it never backs out.
⚠️ ROTATING MECHANISM SAFETY
Planetary gearboxes generate immense mechanical torque. Never insert fingers, pencils, or screwdrivers into moving gears or wheels. When testing motors on your desk, place the robot chassis on a wooden support block so the drive wheels spin freely in the air!
🔧 TROUBLESHOOTING: WHEEL WOBBLE OR CHASSIS RUBBING
If the 100mm rubber tire rubs against the aluminum channel or wobbles as it rotates:
  • Ensure the steel hex coupler is pressed flush against the outer ball bearing face, but leaves a 1.0 mm clearance gap from the channel wall.
  • Check the four M3 screws holding the wheel to the hex hub: tighten them in a crisscross pattern with equal tension.
wiring:
1. Motor & Encoder Wiring Harness to Titan Controller

The Maverick gearmotor features a unified 6-wire harness:

  • Red (+) & Black (-): Heavy-gauge motor armature power leads.
  • Yellow (Ch A) & White (Ch B): Quadrature encoder pulse channels.
  • Blue (+5V) & Green (GND): Regulated logic power for the Hall encoder sensor.

title: Power and Wiring Hygiene
objective: Complete the robot's 12V electrical system using a 3000mAh NiMH battery, 20A blade fuse, main toggle switch, Titan screw terminals, XT60 connectors, and professional wiring hygiene.
exitTicket: What catastrophic failure occurs if battery leads are connected in reverse polarity (Red to Black)?
What is the purpose of the 20-Amp automotive blade fuse in the positive battery line?
Why are high-current motor cables bundled separately from low-voltage sensor cables?
concept:
1. Power Distribution Topology: Muscle vs. Brain

Robots draw significant electrical currents when starting up or pushing against obstacles—up to 15–20 Amps peak per motor! If high-power motors share an unregulated wire with a microprocessor, the sudden current surge will cause a voltage dip (brownout), causing the Raspberry Pi to instantly crash and reboot.

To prevent electrical interference and brownouts, our robot uses a strictly segregated power tree:

[12V 3000mAh Battery (XT60)] 
           │
           ▼
    [20A Blade Fuse]
           │
           ▼
 [Main Power Toggle Switch]

2. Circuit Protection: The 20A Blade Fuse

If a motor stalls or a wire shorts out against the aluminum chassis, the battery can discharge hundreds of amps in milliseconds, melting wires or creating a fire hazard. The 20-Amp automotive blade fuse acts as the electrical guardian: if current ever exceeds 20 Amps, the internal metal element safely melts in milliseconds, disconnecting the battery instantly.

💡 PRO-TIP: MULTIMETER POLARITY AUDIT BEFORE FLIPPING THE SWITCH
Professional robotics engineers follow one unbreakable rule: Never turn on power until you have checked voltage with a multimeter! Set your digital multimeter to DC Volts ($20\,\text{V}$ range). Place the Black probe on the Titan GND terminal and the Red probe on the VIN terminal. It must read between $+12.0\,\text{V}$ and $+13.5\,\text{V}$. If it shows a minus sign ($-12\,\text{V}$), your wires are reversed!
⚠️ REVERSE POLARITY DESTROYS ELECTRONICS INSTANTLY
Reversing polarity (connecting Red $+$ to Black $-$) will permanently fry the MOSFET transistors inside the Titan Quad controller in less than 5 milliseconds! Yellow XT60 battery connectors are physically keyed with chamfered corners to make backward connection impossible. Never force an XT60 connector backward!
🔧 TROUBLESHOOTING: SWITCH IS ON BUT ZERO LEDS LIGHT UP
If you flip the main power switch ON and neither the VMX nor Titan shows any lights:
  1. Check the 20A fuse: Pull the blade fuse from its inline rubber holder and hold it up to the light. If the metal filament inside is broken or charred, replace it with a fresh 20A yellow fuse.
  2. Screw terminal insulation clamp: Inspect where the 14 AWG power wires enter the Titan screw terminals. Ensure the screw is clamping onto bare copper wire, NOT on the plastic insulation jacket!

1. Power System Assembly Procedure

  1. Insert 20A Fuse: Insert the 20-Amp automotive blade fuse into the inline rubber fuse holder on the positive (Red) battery harness lead.
  2. Mount Main Toggle Switch: Secure the heavy-duty SPST toggle switch into the pre-drilled bracket at the rear of the chassis using its threaded lock ring.
  3. Connect Titan Power Terminals: Strip 6mm of insulation from the 14 AWG silicone power leads. Insert the Red lead into VIN (+) and the Black lead into GND (-) on the Titan screw terminal block. Tighten firmly with a flathead screwdriver.
  4. Connect VMX Auxiliary Power: Connect the 2-pin regulated 12V output cable from the Titan to the VMX-pi power input header.
  5. Install Battery Strap: Thread the heavy-duty hook-and-loop strap through the bottom channel slots. Place the 12V 3000mAh NiMH battery pack in the center cavity to ensure a low and balanced center of gravity.

Hands-On Team Challenge: The 5G Tug & Shake Test

🎯 JUNIOR TEAM CHALLENGE: VIBRATION & TUG AUDIT

Perform the rigorous 5G Vibration & Tug Audit on your completed robot with your instructor:

  1. With main power OFF, gently tug every wire connection near the screw terminals and headers. No wire should slip or budge.
  2. Pick up the robot by the side aluminum channels and gently shake it vertically and horizontally. There must be zero rattling, zero loose screws, and zero dangling wires.
  3. Turn the main power switch ON: observe that both the VMX-pi and Titan controller power LEDs remain solid without flickering.
